title: USMNT 6, Haiti 0: No ill effects of Pochettino exit news in Nations League rout
content:
MIAMI — Christian Pulisic scored twice in his return to the national team as the United States dominated Haiti en route to a 6-0 win in the first leg of the Concacaf Nations League quarterfinals.

The team’s first competitive match since being eliminated by Belgium at the World Cup sets up a stress-free second leg in Cincinnati on Tuesday. The win was also the penultimate match of the Mauricio Pochettino era, as he will leave to become head coach at Manchester United after Tuesday’s return leg against Haiti.

Auston Trusty opened the scoring in the first half with a volley from a set piece delivered by Sebastian Berhalter. The USMNT turned control (73% possession in the first half) into dominance in the second half, with Julian Hall scoring the second goal followed by Pulisic scoring a double in under two minutes after the break.

With the result well in hand, Weston McKennie scored a header from a corner kick for the fifth and Folarin Balogun added a sixth later. Like Pulisic, McKennie and Balogun also made their returns to the national team after missing the fall camp.

Here are our writers’ thoughts on the rout, which, in addition to putting one U.S. foot in the March semifinals, also puts the U.S. on the cusp of Gold Cup qualification:

Center back Chris Richards told The Athletic this week, amid rumors swirling of Pochettino’s impending departure, that it was “business as usual” for the USMNT. The group personified those words on Saturday, with a convincing and controlled 6-0 win.

The story of Pochettino to United dominated global soccer news all week, thrusting the players in the middle of it. By Friday morning, Manchester United made it official, but all parties agreed to allow Pochettino coach the USMNT this window for his final two games.

On the field, you’d never know anything was going on. The team was locked in. Pochettino’s demeanor on the sideline was typical for his time with the United States.

Pulisic was lively and took over in the second half, his through ball to Antonee Robinson the catalyst for Hall’s goal then scoring the next two in rapid fashion. For any talk about the future of the program with a crop of hugely exciting teenagers, Pulisic reminded fans about the present.

As for Pochettino’s tactics, the U.S. played out a back four again like it did in the fall. This is a departure from the successful World Cup setup, which was a fluid back three.

McKennie, the central midfielder, was nominally the right winger, but in possession, the wide attackers pinched centrally as both fullbacks raced forward to provide width. Adams and Berhalter anchored central midfield as Malik Tillman had license to go forward.

Out of possession the team defended out of a standard 4-4-2, creating havoc via high pressure whenever Haiti tried to build out of the back, which wasn’t often.

When Berhalter’s free kick curled over Haiti’s defensive line and onto the left foot of Trusty, it was an easy finish for the center back, who scored his first international goal at this summer’s World Cup.

For Trusty, though, the goal held special meaning.

The defender announced last month that his father, Walt, passed away. He left Celtic on bereavement leave and, prior to being called in, had not played since a Europa League game on Oct. 15. Trusty posted a tribute to his father on his Instagram account on Oct. 21.

“To wear the Trusty name on the back of my shirt will forever be my greatest honor,” the center back wrote. “I couldn’t be prouder to be your son.”

To get a goal in his first game back on the field since his father’s passing was undoubtedly emotional.

Though there wasn’t much reason at all to panic, any dual-national worry about Julian Hall is officially over. With his appearance against Haiti in a competitive match, combined with his four senior appearances in the fall window, Hall is cap-tied to the USMNT and cannot switch to Poland.

Hall, 18, respectfully left the door open to Poland in interviews but he never showed any desire with his actions. After missing a golden chance from in close in the first half, Hall marked his cap-tying day with a goal, capping off a perfectly executed counterattack.

The Red Bull New York forward made his senior USMNT debut this fall, scoring in each of his first three games and helping lead the team to a perfect four wins from four games to start the 2030 World Cup cycle.

Hall had 16 goals and four assists for RBNY across all competitions this season, a true breakout campaign for the rising star. His club season is over with RBNY missing the MLS playoffs, but he should be one of the first names on Steve Cherundolo’s list for the off-calendar, MLS-heavy U.S. camp being held in December that the U-23 coach will oversee in Pochettino’s place.

The implication of who starts in these quarterfinals no longer holds the same weight it would have if Pochettino wasn’t leaving as coach. But one of the most important position battles to watch before, during and since this summer’s World Cup is in net, and Diego Kochen was first to hold an audition for whichever coach is coming in next.

Matt Freese was the starter for the big games this summer, but his error against Belgium was enormously costly. It highlighted what had been uneven play for Freese at the position since taking over the starting job, and Freese hasn’t done much in MLS play to convince anyone he should be the outright starter.

Pochettino seemed to acknowledge as much in September-October when he brought four goalkeepers to camp and gave each of them one half in the first two games. Kochen then started against Mexico, while Brian Schwake got the start against Canada to close out the window.

On Saturday, in the first official match since the World Cup, it was the 20-year-old Kochen who got the start. The Barcelona product, who is currently on loan with Danish side Lyngby, stepped up in his first big moment, sticking out his right leg to make a big save in a 1-on-1 with midfielder Danley Jean Jacques in the 16th minute to preserve the U.S.’s 1-0 lead.

Kochen had a bad moment in the second half, but was saved by a video review offside call. A long ball over the top put Haiti in behind the back line and the young goalkeeper came out to make a play, but didn’t get to the ball and ended up in no-man’s land. Haiti’s attacking player cut the ball back and played a cross for an easy finish from Lenny Joseph.

Kochen will feel fortunate about the offside call after making the mistake in net late, even in such a decisive win.
